"""Configuration: configs/defaults.yaml overlaid by configs/<client>.yaml (top-level keys).

Client files come in two schemas (docs/adr/0007-config-schema-v2.md). Schema 1 is flat: every key is
a top-level service key. Schema 2 (`schema: 2`) groups the same keys into sections and is flattened
on load, so the rest of the service only ever sees the flat keys.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import yaml

APP_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CONFIG_DIR = APP_DIR / "configs"
DATA_DIR = APP_DIR / "data"
OUT_DIR = APP_DIR / "out"

# Schema 2: section -> the flat keys it may hold. `name` and `schema` stay at the top level.
V2_SECTIONS = {
    "service": ("interval_minutes", "tz", "operating_hours"),
    "targets": ("sla", "sla_target", "attainment_basis"),
    "staffing": ("queueing", "patience_sec", "occupancy_cap", "aht_smoothing"),
    "scheduling": ("weekly_hours", "max_consecutive_days", "break", "min_cover", "cross_skill_weight"),
}


def _flatten_v2(doc: dict) -> dict:
    """A schema-2 client file -> flat top-level keys. An unknown section or a key in the wrong
    section is an error rather than a silent fall-back to the default."""
    flat = {}
    for key, value in doc.items():
        if key == "schema":
            continue
        if key == "name":
            flat["name"] = value
            continue
        if key not in V2_SECTIONS:
            raise SystemExit(f"config schema 2: unknown section '{key}'")
        for k, v in (value or {}).items():
            if k not in V2_SECTIONS[key]:
                raise SystemExit(f"config schema 2: '{k}' does not belong in section '{key}'")
            flat[k] = v
    return flat


def load_config(client: str) -> dict:
    defaults = yaml.safe_load((CONFIG_DIR / "defaults.yaml").read_text())
    client_file = CONFIG_DIR / f"{client}.yaml"
    if not client_file.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"unknown client '{client}': no {client_file.relative_to(APP_DIR)}")
    doc = yaml.safe_load(client_file.read_text()) or {}
    if doc.get("schema") == 2:
        doc = _flatten_v2(doc)
    elif "schema" in doc:
        raise SystemExit(f"{client_file.relative_to(APP_DIR)}: unsupported config schema {doc['schema']!r}")
    cfg = dict(defaults)
    cfg.update(doc)
    cfg["client"] = client
    return cfg

    rows = [[r.key, r.status, *registry.period(r), len(r.weeks_served(today)) or md.DASH, f"{r.grain} min", r.tz,
             r.export_layout or md.DASH] for r in recs]
    print(md.text_table(["client", "status", "from", "to", "weeks", "grain", "tz", "export"], rows,
                        align="llllrrll", indent=0))
    return 0


def volume_cmd(args) -> int:
    cfg = load_config(args.client)
    rows = volume.volume_report(cfg, args.first, args.last, min_run=args.min_run)
    print(volume.render(cfg, rows, days=args.days, shape=args.profile), end="")
    if args.csv and rows:
        path = _out(args) / args.client / "reports" / f"volume_{args.first or rows[0].week}_{args.last or rows[-1].week}.csv"
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(volume.to_csv(rows))
        print(f"wrote {path}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


def archive_cmd(args) -> int:
    a = history.archive(args.client, args.week, _out(args))
    print(f"archived {args.client} {args.week} -> {a.path}" + (" (replaced)" if a.replaced else ""))
    return 0


def backfill_cmd(args) -> int:
    """Run and archive every week with a canonical file in the range (always under out/, where
    `run` writes)."""
    wanted = [w for w in volume.week_files(args.client) if _in_range(w, args.first, args.last)]
    if not wanted:
        raise SystemExit(f"no canonical week files for {args.client} in the range")
    for w in wanted:
        res = run(args.client, w)
        history.archive(args.client, w, OUT_DIR)
        print(f"{w}  sla {json.dumps(res['sla'])}  meets_target {res['meets_target']}  hours {res['scheduled_hours']}")
    return 0


def summary_cmd(args) -> int:
    out = _out(args)
    cfg = load_config(args.client)
    s = summary.summarise(history.load(args.client, out, args.first, args.last), cfg.get("sla_target"),
                          args.first, args.last)
    path = out / args.client / "reports" / f"summary_{args.first or s.first}_{args.last or s.last}.md"
    if args.csv:
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.with_suffix(".csv").write_text(summary.to_csv(s))
    _write_report(path, summary.render(s, cfg.get("name")))
    return 0


def compare_cmd(args) -> int:
    out = _out(args)
    cfg = load_config(args.client)
    if args.against:
        a, b = compare.archived_side(args.client, args.against, out), compare.archived_side(args.client, args.week, out)
    else:
        a, b = compare.archived_side(args.client, args.week, out), compare.current_side(args.client, args.week, out)
    c = compare.compare(args.client, a, b, cfg["tz"])
    name = f"compare_{args.week}.md" if a.week == b.week else f"compare_{a.week}_{b.week}.md"
    _write_report(out / args.client / "reports" / name, compare.render(c))
    return 1 if args.fail_on_change and c.changed else 0


def accounts_cmd(args) -> int:
    """Latest archived week of each client in the registry (live and paused by default)."""
    out = _out(args)
    statuses = [args.status] if args.status else ["live", "paused"]
    recs = [r for r in registry.load_registry().values() if r.status in statuses]
    _write_report(out / "reports" / "accounts.md", registry.accounts_table(recs, out))
    return 0


def export_cmd(args) -> int:
    out = _out(args)
    name = args.layout or registry.get(args.client).export_layout
    if name is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"no export_layout for {args.client!r} in clients/registry.yaml: pass --layout")
    cfg, _ev, _segments = _run_outputs(args.client, args.week, out)
    agents = load_agents(args.client)
    for n in sorted(LAYOUTS) if name == "all" else [name]:
        print(export_schedule(out / args.client / "schedule.csv", cfg, args.week, n, out, agents))
    return 0


def notify_cmd(args) -> int:
    out = _out(args)
    cfg, ev, segments = _run_outputs(args.client, args.week, out)
    rec = registry.load_registry().get(args.client)
    earlier = [w for w in history.archived_weeks(args.client, out) if weeks.key(w) < weeks.key(args.week)]
    previous = history.read_eval(history.history_dir(args.client, out) / earlier[-1] / "eval.json") if earlier else None
    written = write_notifications(out, cfg, args.week, ev, segments, load_agents(args.client),
                                  rec.account_manager if rec else None, previous)
    print(f"{len(written)} file(s) under {notify_dir(out, args.client, args.week)}")
    return 0


REPORTS = {"volume": volume_cmd, "archive": archive_cmd, "backfill": backfill_cmd, "summary": summary_cmd,
           "compare": compare_cmd, "accounts": accounts_cmd}


def report_cmd(args) -> int:
    return REPORTS[args.report](args)


def _add_subcommands(sub) -> None:
    out_help = "output root (default out/)"
    c = sub.add_parser("clients", help="list clients from clients/registry.yaml")
    c.add_argument("--status", choices=registry.STATUSES)
    c.add_argument("--active-on", type=_date, metavar="YYYY-MM-DD", help="only clients served on that date")
    c.add_argument("--markdown", action="store_true", help="print the client table as markdown")
    c.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="compare the registry with configs, rosters and data")
    c.add_argument("--data", action="store_true", help="with --check: also run the file checks on every week file")
    c.add_argument("--board", action="store_true", help="weekly ops board for --week (data, run, archive, export, digest)")
    c.add_argument("--week", type=_week, help="the week for --board")
    c.add_argument("--from", dest="first", type=_week, help="with --to: --board over a range of weeks")
    c.add_argument("--to", dest="last", type=_week)
    c.add_argument("--timeline", action="store_true", help="month-by-month lifecycle of each client")
    c.add_argument("--until", type=_date, metavar="YYYY-MM-DD", help="last day shown by --timeline (default today)")
    c.add_argument("--out", help="output root for --board (default out/)")

    rep = sub.add_parser("report", help="weekly volume, evaluation archive, summaries and comparisons")
    rs = rep.add_subparsers(dest="report", required=True)
    v = rs.add_parser("volume", help="weekly volume and file checks from data/<client>/week_*.csv")
    a = rs.add_parser("archive", help="copy out/<client>/eval.json and schedule.csv into out/<client>/history/<week>/")
    b = rs.add_parser("backfill", help="run and archive every week with a canonical file in the range (out/)")
    s = rs.add_parser("summary", help="multi-week summary of the archived weeks")
    cm = rs.add_parser("compare", help="archived run of --week against the current run, or archived --against")
    acc = rs.add_parser("accounts", help="latest archived week of each client, by account manager")
    for p in (v, a, b, s, cm):
        p.add_argument("--client", required=True)
    for p in (v, b, s):
        p.add_argument("--from", dest="first", type=_week)
        p.add_argument("--to", dest="last", type=_week)
    for p in (a, cm):
        p.add_argument("--week", required=True, type=_week)
    for p in (v, a, s, cm, acc):
        p.add_argument("--out", help=out_help)
    v.add_argument("--min-run", type=int, default=2, help="zero-volume intervals in a row to report (default 2)")
    v.add_argument("--days", action="store_true", help="add contacts per local day")
    v.add_argument("--profile", action="store_true", help="add the weekday and intraday profile over the range")
    v.add_argument("--csv", action="store_true", help="also write the per-week rows to out/<client>/reports/")
    s.add_argument("--csv", action="store_true", help="also write the per-week rows as CSV")
    cm.add_argument("--against", type=_week, help="an archived week to compare with instead of the current run")
    cm.add_argument("--fail-on-change", action="store_true", help="exit 1 if the schedule or the eval differs")
    acc.add_argument("--status", choices=registry.STATUSES, help="default: live and paused")

    e = sub.add_parser("export", help="write the last run's schedule in an ACD layout")
    e.add_argument("--client", required=True)
    e.add_argument("--week", required=True, type=_week)
    e.add_argument("--layout", choices=[*sorted(LAYOUTS), "all"],
                   help="; ".join(f"{n}: {lay.summary}" for n, lay in sorted(LAYOUTS.items()))
                   + "; all: every layout. Default: the client's export_layout in the registry")
    e.add_argument("--out", help=out_help)

    n = sub.add_parser("notify", help="write the weekly digest, agent notices and day sheets under out/<client>/notify/")
    n.add_argument("--client", required=True)
    n.add_argument("--week", required=True, type=_week)
    n.add_argument("--out", help=out_help)


COMMANDS = {"clients": clients_cmd, "report": report_cmd, "export": export_cmd, "notify": notify_cmd}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wfm", description="Workforce-management service CLI")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    r = sub.add_parser("run", help="ingest -> staffing -> schedule -> evaluate for one client-week")
    r.add_argument("--client", required=True)
    r.add_argument("--week", required=True, help="ISO week, e.g. 2026-W44")

    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if args.cmd == "run":

                                               "scheduled_hours", "agents_scheduled", "violations")}))

    main()
"""Ingest: a client's weekly demand file -> canonical intervals (UTC, client grain).

Two input layouts are supported in data/<client>/:
  week_<ISO>.csv    canonical (client, queue, interval_start_utc, interval_minutes, volume, aht_sec)
  export_<ISO>.csv  a client's own local-time export (interval_start_local, ..., queue, volume, aht_sec),
                    kept from Fabrikam's first onboarding; assumed to be at the client's configured grain.

The result has one row per queue per interval of the ISO week in the client's timezone, at the
client's configured grain, sorted by interval then queue.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, timedelta

import pandas as pd

from wfm.config import DATA_DIR

QUEUES = ("priority", "standard")


def iso_week_monday(week: str) -> date:
    """'2026-W44' -> Monday 2026-10-26."""
    year, wk = week.split("-W")
    return date.fromisocalendar(int(year), int(wk), 1)


def local_days(week: str, tz: str) -> list[date]:
    mon = iso_week_monday(week)
    return [mon + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(7)]


def _read_canonical(path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.read_csv(path)
    df["interval_start_utc"] = pd.to_datetime(df["interval_start_utc"], utc=True)
    return df[["queue", "interval_start_utc", "volume", "aht_sec"]]


# Fabrikam's re-sent 2025 exports have no offset column. US Eastern offset in effect from each DST
# change date (local) on; good enough for Fabrikam's weeks (WFM-204).
FABRIKAM_OFFSETS = {"2025-03-09": "-04:00", "2025-11-02": "-05:00", "2026-03-08": "-04:00", "2026-11-01": "-05:00"}


def _fixed_offsets(local: pd.Series, table: dict[str, str]) -> pd.Series:
    """UTC from local wall-clock labels and a {change date: offset} table."""
    keys = sorted(table)
    off = [table[max([k for k in keys if k <= d] or keys[:1])] for d in local.dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")]
    return pd.to_datetime(local.dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M") + pd.Series(off, index=local.index),
                          format="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M%z", utc=True)


def _read_export(path, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.read_csv(path)
    local = pd.to_datetime(df["interval_start_local"])
    if cfg["client"] == "fabrikam" and "utc_offset" not in df:   # WFM-204
        df["interval_start_utc"] = _fixed_offsets(local, FABRIKAM_OFFSETS)
    else:
        df["interval_start_utc"] = local.dt.tz_localize(cfg["tz"]).dt.tz_convert("UTC")
    return df[["queue", "interval_start_utc", "volume", "aht_sec"]]


def _resample(df: pd.DataFrame, grain_min: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Aggregate to the configured grain: volume summed, AHT volume-weighted."""
    df = df.copy()
    df["interval_start_utc"] = df["interval_start_utc"].dt.floor(f"{grain_min}min")
    df["_w"] = df["volume"] * df["aht_sec"]
    g = df.groupby(["queue", "interval_start_utc"], sort=True).agg(
        volume=("volume", "sum"), _w=("_w", "sum"), aht_mean=("aht_sec", "mean")).reset_index()
    g["aht_sec"] = (g["_w"] / g["volume"]).where(g["volume"] > 0, g["aht_mean"])
    return g[["queue", "interval_start_utc", "volume", "aht_sec"]]


def load_week(cfg: dict, week: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    client = cfg["client"]
    grain = cfg["interval_minutes"]
    canon = DATA_DIR / client / f"week_{week}.csv"
    export = DATA_DIR / client / f"export_{week}.csv"
    if canon.exists():
        df = _read_canonical(canon)
    elif export.exists():
        df = _read_export(export, cfg)
    else:
        raise SystemExit(f"no data for {client} {week}: expected {canon} or {export}")

    df = _resample(df, grain)
    grid = pd.DatetimeIndex(sorted(df["interval_start_utc"].unique()))   # the week as the data delivers it
    frames = []
    for q in QUEUES:
        part = df[df["queue"] == q].set_index("interval_start_utc").reindex(grid)
        part["queue"] = q
        part["volume"] = part["volume"].fillna(0.0)
        part["aht_sec"] = part["aht_sec"].fillna(part["aht_sec"].mean())
        frames.append(part.rename_axis("interval_start_utc").reset_index())
    out = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    out["client"] = client
    out["interval_minutes"] = grain
    out = out.sort_values(["interval_start_utc", "queue"], kind="stable").reset_index(drop=True)
    return out[["client", "queue", "interval_start_utc", "interval_minutes", "volume", "aht_sec"]]

"""Erlang C staffing maths. Pure Python, no dependencies.

Used by wfm.staffing.required to turn interval volume and handle time into required agents.

Conventions
-----------
volume        contacts arriving in the interval
interval_sec  interval length in seconds
aht_sec       average handle time in seconds (talk + wrap)
target_sec    service-level answer-time target (e.g. 20 for "80/20")
sl_target     service-level fraction (e.g. 0.80)
occupancy_cap max A/N allowed (e.g. 0.85); None disables the cap

Sanity check (standard calculator figure): 1,000 calls/hour, AHT 180 s, 80% in 20 s -> 56 agents.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math


def traffic_intensity(volume: float, interval_sec: float, aht_sec: float) -> float:
    """Erlangs: arrival rate x handle time."""
    if interval_sec <= 0 or aht_sec <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return (volume / interval_sec) * aht_sec


def erlang_c_prob_wait(a: float, n: int) -> float:
    """Probability that an arriving contact must wait, with traffic a Erlangs and n agents.

    Returns 1.0 when n <= a (unstable queue). Terms are accumulated iteratively to avoid
    overflow in a**n / n! for large n.
    """
    if a <= 0:
        return 0.0
    if n <= a:
        return 1.0
    term = 1.0          # a^0 / 0!
    s = 1.0             # sum_{k=0}^{n-1} a^k / k!
    for k in range(1, n):
        term *= a / k
        s += term
    term *= a / n       # a^n / n!
    top = term * n / (n - a)
    return top / (s + top)


def service_level(a: float, n: int, aht_sec: float, target_sec: float) -> float:
    """Fraction of contacts answered within target_sec."""
    if a <= 0:
        return 1.0
    if n <= a:
        return 0.0
    pw = erlang_c_prob_wait(a, n)
    return 1.0 - pw * math.exp(-(n - a) * target_sec / aht_sec)


def asa(a: float, n: int, aht_sec: float) -> float:
    """Average speed of answer in seconds."""
    if a <= 0:
        return 0.0
    if n <= a:
        return float("inf")
    return erlang_c_prob_wait(a, n) * aht_sec / (n - a)


def occupancy(a: float, n: int) -> float:
    return 0.0 if n <= 0 else a / n


def required_agents(
    volume: float,
    interval_sec: float,
    aht_sec: float,
    sl_target: float,
    target_sec: float,
    occupancy_cap: float | None = None,
    max_agents: int = 2000,
) -> int:
    """Smallest n meeting the service-level target and (if given) the occupancy cap."""
    a = traffic_intensity(volume, interval_sec, aht_sec)
    if a <= 0:
        return 0
    n = max(1, math.ceil(a))
    while n < max_agents:
        ok_sl = service_level(a, n, aht_sec, target_sec) >= sl_target
        ok_occ = occupancy_cap is None or occupancy(a, n) <= occupancy_cap
        if ok_sl and ok_occ:
            return n
        n += 1
    return n


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Standard check: 1000 calls/hour, AHT 180 s, 80/20 -> 56 agents
    n = required_agents(volume=1000, interval_sec=3600, aht_sec=180, sl_target=0.80, target_sec=20)
    a = traffic_intensity(1000, 3600, 180)
    print(f"A={a:.2f} Erlangs, required={n}, SL={service_level(a, n, 180, 20):.3f}, "
          f"ASA={asa(a, n, 180):.1f}s, occ={occupancy(a, n):.3f}")
    assert n == 56, n
    # With an occupancy cap the answer can only go up
    n2 = required_agents(1000, 3600, 180, 0.80, 20, occupancy_cap=0.85)
    assert n2 >= n
    print("ok")
"""Staffing: required agents per queue per interval (Erlang C at the client's SLA targets)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd

from vendor.qlib import required_agents as qlib_required
from wfm.staffing.erlang import required_agents


def _handle_time(g: pd.DataFrame, mode: str) -> pd.Series:
    """Handle time per interval under the configured smoothing (`aht_smoothing`):
    `queue_mean` (default) — the queue's mean AHT over intervals with volume; `interval` — each row's own AHT."""
    if mode == "interval":
        return g["aht_sec"]
    return pd.Series(g.loc[g["volume"] > 0, "aht_sec"].mean(), index=g.index)


def _model(cfg: dict):
    """Queueing model for required staffing (`queueing`): `erlang` — wfm/staffing/erlang.py, the
    service default; `qlib` — vendor/qlib with caller abandonment (Fabrikam), patience from
    `patience_sec` or the library default."""
    if cfg.get("queueing", "erlang") == "qlib":
        patience = cfg.get("patience_sec")
        return lambda v, sec, aht, target, seconds, cap=None: qlib_required(v, sec, aht, target, seconds, cap,
                                                                             patience_sec=patience)
    return required_agents


def add_required(df: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Append a `required` column to the canonical intervals frame."""
    interval_sec = cfg["interval_minutes"] * 60
    model = _model(cfg)
    cap = cfg.get("occupancy_cap")  # WFM-212: read here, not yet applied in the call below
    mode = cfg.get("aht_smoothing", "queue_mean")
    out = df.copy()
    out["required"] = 0
    for q, g in out.groupby("queue", sort=False):
        sla = cfg["sla"][q]
        # per-interval AHT is too noisy at low volume; use the smoothed queue AHT (WFM-198)
        aht = float(_handle_time(g, mode)[g["volume"] > 0].mean())
        out.loc[g.index, "required"] = [
            model(v, interval_sec, aht, sla["target"], sla["seconds"]) for v in g["volume"]
        ]
    out.attrs["occupancy_cap"] = cap
    return out
"""Minimum cover: queues that need a number of agents on shift whatever the volume.

A client config names them under `min_cover`, with the local hours the floor applies:

    min_cover:
      chat: {agents: 2, hours: [20, 24]}

The scheduler raises each interval's requirement on the queue to the floor; the evaluator reports
intervals below it as `min_cover` violations.

Cross-skilled cover (PR #31). An agent on shift on another queue who also holds the floor queue's
skill counts `cross_skill_weight` of an agent toward the floor (service default 0.5: a voice agent
with the chat skill picks up chats between calls). The weight applies to the floor only; required
agents from the staffing model are always counted on the queue itself.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo


def floor(queue: str, t: datetime, cfg: dict) -> int:
    """Agents the floor asks for on `queue` in the interval starting at `t` (0 if none applies)."""
    rule = (cfg.get("min_cover") or {}).get(queue)
    if not rule:
        return 0
    loc = t.astimezone(ZoneInfo(cfg["tz"]))
    h = loc.hour + loc.minute / 60
    lo, hi = rule.get("hours", cfg["operating_hours"])
    return int(rule["agents"]) if lo <= h < hi else 0


def weight(cfg: dict) -> float:
    return float(cfg.get("cross_skill_weight", 0.0))


def cover(on_queue: float, cross_skilled: float, cfg: dict) -> float:
    """Cover counted toward a floor: agents on the queue plus weighted cross-skilled agents elsewhere."""
    return on_queue + weight(cfg) * cross_skilled


def uncovered(required: int, floor_need: int, on_queue: float, cross_skilled: float, cfg: dict) -> float:
    """What the interval still lacks: the staffing requirement (agents on the queue) or the floor
    (cover as above), whichever is short by more."""
    return max(0.0, required - on_queue, floor_need - cover(on_queue, cross_skilled, cfg))

Used by wfm.staffing.required to turn interval volume and handle time into required agents.

Conventions
-----------
volume        contacts arriving in the interval

"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math


def traffic_intensity(volume: float, interval_sec: float, aht_sec: float) -> float:
    """Erlangs: arrival rate x handle time."""
    if interval_sec <= 0 or aht_sec <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return (volume / interval_sec) * aht_sec


def erlang_c_prob_wait(a: float, n: int) -> float:
    """Probability that an arriving contact must wait, with traffic a Erlangs and n agents.

    Returns 1.0 when n <= a (unstable queue). Terms are accumulated iteratively to avoid
    overflow in a**n / n! for large n.
    """
    if a <= 0:
        return 0.0
    if n <= a:
        return 1.0
    term = 1.0          # a^0 / 0!
    s = 1.0             # sum_{k=0}^{n-1} a^k / k!
    for k in range(1, n):
        term *= a / k
        s += term
    term *= a / n       # a^n / n!
    top = term * n / (n - a)
    return top / (s + top)


def service_level(a: float, n: int, aht_sec: float, target_sec: float) -> float:
    """Fraction of contacts answered within target_sec."""
    if a <= 0:
        return 1.0
    if n <= a:
        return 0.0
    pw = erlang_c_prob_wait(a, n)

    if a <= 0:
        return 0.0
    if n <= a:

    return erlang_c_prob_wait(a, n) * aht_sec / (n - a)

"""Shift templates: local wall-clock segments on one local day; none crosses local midnight."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Template:
    id: str
    segments: tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]  # (start_hour, end_hour) local, end may be 24
    eligibility: str = "all"               # "all" or a contract code

    @property
    def hours(self) -> float:
        return float(sum(e - s for s, e in self.segments))

    @property
    def is_split(self) -> bool:
        return len(self.segments) > 1

    def segments_utc(self, day: date, tz: str) -> list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]:
        """Local wall-clock segments on `day` -> UTC datetimes."""
        z = ZoneInfo(tz)
        midnight = datetime(day.year, day.month, day.day, tzinfo=z)
        return [((midnight + timedelta(hours=s)).astimezone(timezone.utc),
                 (midnight + timedelta(hours=e)).astimezone(timezone.utc)) for s, e in self.segments]


TEMPLATES: list[Template] = [
    Template("E8", ((6, 14),)),
    Template("D8", ((9, 17),)),
    Template("L8", ((13, 21),)),
    Template("N8", ((16, 24),)),
    Template("P6a", ((7, 13),)),
    Template("P6b", ((15, 21),)),
    Template("P4", ((10, 14),)),
    Template("S44", ((8, 12), (16, 20)), eligibility="all"),
]


def templates_for(cfg: dict) -> list[Template]:
    """Templates that fit inside the client's local operating hours."""
    open_h, close_h = cfg["operating_hours"]
    return [t for t in TEMPLATES if all(open_h <= s and e <= close_h for s, e in t.segments)]


def eligible(template: Template, contract: str) -> bool:
    return template.eligibility == "all" or template.eligibility == contract
"""Greedy template placement, one local day at a time.

For each local day of the week: while some (template, queue) pair still covers at least half an
hour of uncovered requirement, place the best-scoring pair on the available agent with the fewest
hours so far. Breaks go at the shift midpoint. Deterministic: fixed template order, agent ids as
the tie-break.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pandas as pd

from wfm import constraints
from wfm.ingest.loader import local_days
from wfm.roster import Agent
from wfm.scheduler.templates import Template, eligible, templates_for


@dataclass
class Shift:
    agent_id: str
    queue: str
    template: Template
    day: date
    segments: list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]
    intervals: list[datetime] = field(default_factory=list)   # grid slots the segments cover
    break_start: datetime | None = None
    break_minutes: int = 0

    @property
    def hours(self) -> float:
        return sum((e - s).total_seconds() for s, e in self.segments) / 3600.0

hour of uncovered requirement, place the best-scoring pair on the available agent with the fewest
hours so far. Breaks go at the shift midpoint. Deterministic: fixed template order, agent ids as
the tie-break.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pandas as pd

from wfm import constraints
from wfm.ingest.loader import local_days
from wfm.roster import Agent
from wfm.scheduler.templates import Template, eligible, templates_for


@dataclass
class Shift:
    agent_id: str
    queue: str
    template: Template
    day: date
    segments: list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]
    intervals: list[datetime] = field(default_factory=list)   # grid slots the segments cover
    break_start: datetime | None = None
    break_minutes: int = 0

    @property
    def hours(self) -> float:
        return sum((e - s).total_seconds() for s, e in self.segments) / 3600.0


def _covered(segments, day_grid) -> list[datetime]:
    return [t for s, e in segments for t in day_grid if s <= t < e]


def schedule_week(req: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent], week: str) -> list[Shift]:
    tz = cfg["tz"]
    grain_h = cfg["interval_minutes"] / 60.0
    caps = cfg["weekly_hours"]
    max_run = cfg["max_consecutive_days"]
    templates = templates_for(cfg)
    queues = list(dict.fromkeys(req["queue"]))

    required = {q: dict(zip(g["interval_start_utc"], g["required"])) for q, g in req.groupby("queue")}
    cover = {q: defaultdict(int) for q in queues}
    cross = {q: defaultdict(int) for q in queues}    # agents on another queue holding this skill (min_cover)
    grid = sorted(set(req["interval_start_utc"]))
    z = ZoneInfo(tz)
    floors = {q: {t: constraints.floor(q, t, cfg) for t in grid} for q in queues}

    hours_used: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
    days_worked: dict[str, list[date]] = defaultdict(list)
    shifts: list[Shift] = []

    for day in local_days(week, tz):
        day_grid = [t for t in grid if t.astimezone(z).date() == day]
        worked_today: set[str] = set()
        dead: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()   # (template, queue) pairs nobody can take today
        while True:
            best, best_val = None, 0.0
            for tpl in templates:
                segs = tpl.segments_utc(day, tz)
                ivs = _covered(segs, day_grid)
                for q in queues:
                    if (tpl.id, q) in dead:
                        continue
                    val = sum(min(1, constraints.uncovered(required[q][t], floors[q][t], cover[q][t], cross[q][t], cfg))
                              for t in ivs)
                    if val > best_val + 1e-9:
                        best, best_val = (tpl, q, segs, ivs), val
            if best is None or best_val * grain_h < 0.5:
                break
            tpl, q, segs, ivs = best
            cands = [a for a in agents
                     if q in a.skills and eligible(tpl, a.contract) and a.agent_id not in worked_today
                     and hours_used[a.agent_id] + tpl.hours <= caps[a.contract] + 1e-9
                     and not _would_exceed_run(days_worked[a.agent_id], day, max_run)]
            if not cands:
                dead.add((tpl.id, q))
                continue
            a = min(cands, key=lambda x: (hours_used[x.agent_id], x.agent_id))
            shifts.append(Shift(a.agent_id, q, tpl, day, segs, ivs))
            hours_used[a.agent_id] += tpl.hours
            days_worked[a.agent_id].append(day)
            worked_today.add(a.agent_id)
            for t in ivs:
                cover[q][t] += 1
                for other in a.skills & set(queues) - {q}:
                    cross[other][t] += 1

    place_breaks(shifts, cfg)
    return shifts


def _would_exceed_run(worked: list[date], day: date, max_run: int) -> bool:
    """True if working `day` would make more than max_run consecutive local days."""
    run = 0
    d = day - timedelta(days=1)
    while d in worked:
        run += 1
        d -= timedelta(days=1)
    return run >= max_run


def place_breaks(shifts: list[Shift], cfg: dict) -> None:
    """One break per long shift, on the covered interval nearest the shift midpoint."""
    rule = cfg["break"]
    length = timedelta(minutes=rule["minutes"])
    for sh in shifts:
        if sh.hours < rule["min_shift_hours"]:
            continue
        fits = [t for t in sh.intervals if any(s <= t and t + length <= e for s, e in sh.segments)]
        if not fits:
            continue
        mid = sh.segments[0][0] + timedelta(hours=sh.hours / 2)
        sh.break_start = min(fits, key=lambda t: (abs((t - mid).total_seconds()), t))
        sh.break_minutes = rule["minutes"]


def to_frame(shifts: list[Shift]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """schedule.csv rows: one per segment; the break sits on the segment that contains it."""
    rows = []
    for sh in shifts:
        for i, (s, e) in enumerate(sh.segments):
            has_break = sh.break_start is not None and s <= sh.break_start < e
            rows.append({
                "agent_id": sh.agent_id, "queue": sh.queue,
                "segment_start_utc": s.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
                "segment_end_utc": e.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
                "template_id": sh.template.id, "segment_idx": i,
                "break_start_utc": sh.break_start.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") if has_break else "",
                "break_minutes": sh.break_minutes if has_break else 0,
            })
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["agent_id", "queue", "segment_start_utc", "segment_end_utc",
                                     "template_id", "segment_idx", "break_start_utc", "break_minutes"])
    return df.sort_values(["segment_start_utc", "agent_id", "segment_idx"], kind="stable").reset_index(drop=True)
"""Agents: data/agents/<client>.csv -> list of Agent."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pandas as pd

from wfm.config import DATA_DIR


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Agent:
    agent_id: str
    contract: str            # "FT" | "PT"

def load_agents(client: str) -> list[Agent]:

    return [Agent(r.agent_id, r.contract, frozenset(r.skills.split(";"))) for r in df.itertuples(index=False)]

"""Staffing helpers built on qlib.models."""
from __future__ import annotations

from .models import DEFAULT_PATIENCE_SEC, carried_traffic, service_level


def traffic(volume: float, interval_sec: float, aht_sec: float) -> float:
    if interval_sec <= 0 or aht_sec <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return volume * aht_sec / interval_sec


def achieved(volume: float, interval_sec: float, aht_sec: float, agents: int, target_sec: float,
             patience_sec: float | None = None) -> float:
    """Service level `agents` achieve on an interval's volume."""
    p = DEFAULT_PATIENCE_SEC if patience_sec is None else patience_sec
    return service_level(traffic(volume, interval_sec, aht_sec), agents, aht_sec, target_sec, p)


def required_agents(volume: float, interval_sec: float, aht_sec: float, sl_target: float, target_sec: float,
                    occupancy_cap: float | None = None, patience_sec: float | None = None,
                    max_agents: int = 2000) -> int:
    """Smallest n whose service level meets sl_target and whose occupancy (carried traffic / n)
    is within occupancy_cap. patience_sec=None uses the library default."""
    p = DEFAULT_PATIENCE_SEC if patience_sec is None else patience_sec
    a = traffic(volume, interval_sec, aht_sec)
    if a <= 0:
        return 0
    n = 1
    while n < max_agents:
        if service_level(a, n, aht_sec, target_sec, p) >= sl_target:
            if occupancy_cap is None or carried_traffic(a, n, aht_sec, p) / n <= occupancy_cap:

    return n

# 0002 — Store UTC, plan in local wall-clock time

Date: 2024-11-15 · Status: accepted · Author: Dana Vexley

## Context

Clients sit in different timezones and most of them change offset twice a year. Agents work local
shifts ("09:00 to 17:00"), contracts count hours worked, and the platform exports we receive are
stamped in whatever the client's platform uses.

## Decision

- Every timestamp the service stores or writes is UTC (`*_utc` columns, ISO 8601 with `Z`).
- Shift templates are local wall-clock segments on one local day and never cross local midnight. A
  template becomes UTC per day through the client's IANA timezone (`tz`).
- Durations (shift length, weekly hours, rest) are elapsed time, measured in UTC.
- The planning week is the ISO week in the client's local time: local Monday 00:00 to the next local
  Monday 00:00.

## Consequences

- A week that contains a DST change has a different number of intervals: one hour fewer in spring,
  one more in autumn. Code that assumes 7 × 24 hours per week is wrong for those weeks.
- A template that spanned the change night would be an hour shorter or longer in elapsed time. The
  templates in use start at 06:00 local or later, so this does not arise today.
- Reports and exports for people convert back to local time at the edge, per row.
# 0003 — Deterministic scheduling

Date: 2024-11-21 · Status: accepted · Author: Dana Vexley

## Context

Weekly schedules are compared with the previous week, re-run after data corrections and reviewed as
diffs. A planner that gives a different answer on every run makes all three useless: a reviewer
cannot tell a change caused by new data from noise.

## Decision

- No randomness in planning code. Template order is fixed; ties between agents are broken by
  `agent_id`; every output is sorted before it is written.
- The same inputs (data file, config, roster, code) give byte-identical `schedule.csv` and `eval.json`.
- Anything outside the service that needs random numbers (synthetic test data, sampling) takes an
  explicit seed.

## Consequences

- Re-running a week after a fix shows exactly what the fix changed; `diff` is the review tool.
- The greedy placement does not search, so it can miss better schedules. A future solver must keep this
  property: fixed seeds, stable sorts, no dependence on dictionary or set iteration order.
# 0007 — Client config schema 2

Date: 2025-11-10 · Status: accepted · Author: Tomas Okafor

## Context

Flat client files (0004) mix planning grain, service targets and contract rules in one list of keys.
Proseware's onboarding sheet arrives in sections (service hours, targets, working-time rules) and maps
onto those keys badly. A typo in a flat file (`operating_hour:`) is silently ignored and the client
gets the default.

## Decision

Schema 2 groups the same keys into four sections. A file declares `schema: 2` at the top:

```yaml
schema: 2
name: Proseware
service:                 # grain, timezone, operating hours
  interval_minutes: 30
  tz: Europe/Berlin
  operating_hours: [7, 21]
targets:                 # service-level targets and the evaluator's settings
  sla:
    priority: {target: 0.85, seconds: 20}
    standard: {target: 0.80, seconds: 30}
staffing: {}             # staffing-model settings
scheduling:              # working-time rules
  weekly_hours: {FT: 39, PT: 20}
```

- Keys inside a section are exactly the flat keys; `V2_SECTIONS` in `wfm/config.py` lists which keys
  each section may hold. `load_config` flattens a schema-2 file (`_flatten_v2`) before the overlay, so
  the rest of the service sees flat keys only.
- An unknown section, or a key in the wrong section, stops the run with an error naming it.
- Schema-1 files load exactly as before. Existing clients are not migrated.
- New clients from Proseware on are written in schema 2.

## Consequences

- One flat namespace underneath: a key cannot mean two things in two sections.
- The overlay rule is unchanged: a nested value such as `sla` replaces the default whole.
- Adding a service key means adding it to its section in `V2_SECTIONS`, or schema-2 clients cannot set it.
# 0005 — Vendoring third-party code

Date: 2025-08-08 · Status: accepted · Author: Mei Lindqvist

## Context

The Fabrikam pilot, starting 2025-08-11, plans with a queueing model that includes caller abandonment.
The service's own Erlang C (`wfm/staffing/erlang.py`) has none. qlib, a small MIT-licensed queueing
library, provides one. The service's runtime dependencies are pandas, numpy and pyyaml, pinned, and we
want to keep it that way.

## Decision

- Third-party code the service runs lives under `vendor/<name>/` and is imported as `vendor.<name>`.
- Only pure-Python packages without dependencies of their own are vendored.
- Each vendored package keeps its `LICENSE`, its `README.md` (stating the version), its `CHANGELOG.md`
  and its own tests; `python -m pytest -q vendor/<name>/tests` passes.
- No local edits inside `vendor/`. A change the service needs goes upstream or into a wrapper under
  `wfm/`.
- An upgrade replaces the package directory in one commit whose message names the old and the new
  version.

## Consequences

- The service's Erlang C remains the model every client uses by default; a vendored model is chosen
  per client in its config.
- The runtime dependency list stays at three pinned packages.

Same template-placement loop as `greedy.py`, but with week state so that the rules in the newer
contracts (minimum rest between shifts, split shifts only for part-time) are enforced while placing
instead of being audited afterwards.

Status

  [x] rest between shifts (MIN_REST_HOURS; move to config before wiring in)

  [ ] break placement per contract (still the midpoint rule, copied from greedy.py)
  [ ] compare output with greedy.py on Contoso W41–W43; unit tests

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pandas as pd

from wfm.ingest.loader import local_days
from wfm.roster import Agent
from wfm.scheduler.greedy import Shift, _covered, _would_exceed_run
from wfm.scheduler.templates import templates_for

MIN_REST_HOURS = 11.0   # TODO(WFM-231): read from config; 11 h is the figure in the newer contracts


def _rested(last_end: datetime | None, start: datetime, min_rest_hours: float) -> bool:
    """At least `min_rest_hours` between the previous shift's end and this start. No previous shift: ok."""
    return last_end is None or start - last_end < timedelta(hours=min_rest_hours)


def schedule_week(req: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, agents: list[Agent], week: str) -> list[Shift]:
    tz = cfg["tz"]
    grain_h = cfg["interval_minutes"] / 60.0
    caps = cfg["weekly_hours"]
    max_run = cfg["max_consecutive_days"]
    templates = templates_for(cfg)
    queues = list(dict.fromkeys(req["queue"]))

    required = {q: dict(zip(g["interval_start_utc"], g["required"])) for q, g in req.groupby("queue")}
    cover = {q: defaultdict(int) for q in queues}
    grid = sorted(set(req["interval_start_utc"]))
    z = ZoneInfo(tz)

    # week state
    hours_used: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
    days_worked: dict[str, list[date]] = defaultdict(list)
    last_end: dict[str, datetime] = {}
    shifts: list[Shift] = []

    for day in local_days(week, tz):
        day_grid = [t for t in grid if t.astimezone(z).date() == day]
        worked_today: set[str] = set()
        dead: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
        while True:
            best, best_val = None, 0.0
            for tpl in templates:
                segs = tpl.segments_utc(day, tz)
                ivs = _covered(segs, day_grid)
                for q in queues:
                    if (tpl.id, q) in dead:
                        continue
                    val = sum(max(0, min(1, required[q][t] - cover[q][t])) for t in ivs)
                    if val > best_val + 1e-9:
                        best, best_val = (tpl, q, segs, ivs), val
            if best is None or best_val * grain_h < 0.5:
                break
            tpl, q, segs, ivs = best
            cands = [a for a in agents
                     if q in a.skills and a.agent_id not in worked_today
                     and (not tpl.is_split or a.contract == "PT")
                     and hours_used[a.agent_id] + tpl.hours <= caps[a.contract] + 1e-9
                     and not _would_exceed_run(days_worked[a.agent_id], day, max_run)
                     and _rested(last_end.get(a.agent_id), segs[0][0], MIN_REST_HOURS)]
            if not cands:
                dead.add((tpl.id, q))
                continue
            a = min(cands, key=lambda x: (hours_used[x.agent_id], x.agent_id))
            shifts.append(Shift(a.agent_id, q, tpl, day, segs, ivs))
            hours_used[a.agent_id] += tpl.hours
            days_worked[a.agent_id].append(day)
            last_end[a.agent_id] = segs[-1][1]
            worked_today.add(a.agent_id)
            for t in ivs:
                cover[q][t] += 1

    _place_breaks_midpoint(shifts, cfg)
    return shifts


def _place_breaks_midpoint(shifts: list[Shift], cfg: dict) -> None:
    """Copied from greedy.place_breaks. TODO(WFM-231): contract-specific placement."""
    rule = cfg["break"]
    length = timedelta(minutes=rule["minutes"])
    for sh in shifts:
        if sh.hours < rule["min_shift_hours"]:
            continue
        fits = [t for t in sh.intervals if any(s <= t and t + length <= e for s, e in sh.segments)]
        if not fits:
            continue
        mid = sh.segments[0][0] + timedelta(hours=sh.hours / 2)
        sh.break_start = min(fits, key=lambda t: (abs((t - mid).total_seconds()), t))
        sh.break_minutes = rule["minutes"]

"""Staffing helpers built on qlib.models."""
from __future__ import annotations

from .models import DEFAULT_PATIENCE_SEC, carried_traffic, service_level


def traffic(volume: float, interval_sec: float, aht_sec: float) -> float:
    if interval_sec <= 0 or aht_sec <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return volume * aht_sec / interval_sec


def achieved(volume: float, interval_sec: float, aht_sec: float, agents: int, target_sec: float,
             patience_sec: float | None = None) -> float:
    """Service level `agents` achieve on an interval's volume."""
    p = DEFAULT_PATIENCE_SEC if patience_sec is None else patience_sec
    return service_level(traffic(volume, interval_sec, aht_sec), agents, aht_sec, target_sec, p)


def required_agents(volume: float, interval_sec: float, aht_sec: float, sl_target: float, target_sec: float,
                    occupancy_cap: float | None = None, patience_sec: float | None = None,
                    max_agents: int = 2000) -> int:
    """Smallest n whose service level meets sl_target and whose occupancy (carried traffic / n)
    is within occupancy_cap. patience_sec=None uses the library default."""
    p = DEFAULT_PATIENCE_SEC if patience_sec is None else patience_sec
    a = traffic(volume, interval_sec, aht_sec)

    n = 1

        if service_level(a, n, aht_sec, target_sec, p) >= sl_target:
            if occupancy_cap is None or carried_traffic(a, n, aht_sec, p) / n <= occupancy_cap:
                return n
        n += 1
    return n

# 2025-11-03 — Woodgrove 2025-W44 ingested an hour off after the fall-back

Week: 2025-W44 (27 October – 2 November 2025; US clocks went back at 02:00 on Sunday 2 November) ·
Written: 2025-11-05 · Author: Tomas Okafor · WFM-114

## Summary

Woodgrove's platform exports interval data in Pacific wall-clock time without an offset column. The
converter that turns that export into the canonical file took the offset of the file's first row
(UTC−7) and applied it to the whole week. Every row from the repeated 01:00 hour on Sunday was stamped
an hour early in UTC.

## Impact

- The converted file had 336 distinct interval starts instead of 338, and two duplicated ones (the
  repeated 01:00 hour, which carries no volume).
- Sunday's demand landed an hour early against the templates: the 06:00 opening hour showed volume
  from 05:00, outside operating hours, and Sunday's attainment came out well below the rest of the week.
- The Monday run's export went to Woodgrove before the problem was found and was replaced on
  Wednesday 5 November.

## Detection

The drop check and the commit were skipped that Monday (rota handover): the converted file was run and
exported straight from the drop folder. Joel Mbeki's digest review flagged Sunday's attainment the same
afternoon, and `python -m wfm report volume` on the file then showed 336 intervals against 338
expected.

## Resolution

- The converter now takes each row's offset from the timezone database for the row's local time, and
  resolves the repeated hour by row order (first occurrence UTC−7, second UTC−8).
- 2025-W44 was re-cut and committed on 2025-11-05 with 338 intervals, re-run and re-exported.
- Same weekend, other clients: Adatum's 2025-W44 file (America/Denver, hourly) had the expected 169
  intervals. Tailspin's autumn change (Europe/Dublin, 2025-W43) had come through with 338 intervals.
----
# 0008 — Client lifecycle and the registry

Date: 2026-10-14 · Status: accepted · Author: Tomas Okafor

## Context

Three clients have retired (Tailspin 2025-10-31, Woodgrove 2026-01-16, Adatum 2026-03-27), Proseware
paused at its own request on 2026-08-14, and Northwind is signed for 2026-W44. Status lived in
people's heads and in the weekly ops list. The same questions kept coming back: can a retired client's
files go, should a paused client's drops still be committed, when does a new client's config land.

## Decision

- `clients/registry.yaml` records every client with a status: `live`, `paused`, `retired` or
  `onboarding`, the lifecycle dates, grain, timezone, queues, config schema, export layout and account
  manager. `clients/README.md` is the readable view and is kept in step with it.
- **Retired**: config, roster, data and unit tests stay. No weekly runs. `ended` is the last day served.
- **Paused**: everything stays; no weekly runs; `paused_from` is the first day not served. A restart sets
  the status back to `live` and starts with the next data drop.
- **Onboarding**: an entry with `golive_week`. Config and roster land with the go-live change.
- `python -m wfm clients --check` compares the registry with `configs/`, `data/` and the rosters. An
  onboarding client without a config is reported as pending, not as an error.
- Deleting a client's files needs its own decision record.

## Consequences

- The repository keeps growing with retired clients' data, about 1 MB per client-year at a 30-minute
  grain.
- Schema-1 configs stay supported for as long as a retired client uses one.
- `export` takes the client's layout from the registry when `--layout` is not given.
----
# Weekly operations

The weekly cycle for live clients: data drops, runs, exports, digests and the monthly summary. Times
are UTC. Commands run from the service root.

## The week

| when | what |
|---|---|
| Monday, 07:00–09:00 | clients drop the previous week's interval file (exact times in `docs/clients/<client>.md`) |
| Monday | check, commit, run and archive each drop |
| Monday, by 17:00 | exports to the clients' WFM teams, digests to the account managers |
| Tuesday, 12:00 | missing drops chased; the digest goes out marked "data pending" |
| first Monday of the month | multi-week summary for the account reviews |

The rota (Dana Vexley, Tomas Okafor, Mei Lindqvist) changes on Mondays. Account managers: Sam Ferreira
(Contoso, Proseware), Ruth Abara (Fabrikam, Wingtip). Joel Mbeki reads every digest before it goes.

## Which clients

`python -m wfm clients --status live` lists this week's clients. Paused and retired clients get no
weekly run (`docs/adr/0008-client-lifecycle.md`). `python -m wfm clients --check` once a week; it
should report nothing. `python -m wfm clients --board --week <week>` shows, per client, the next open
step for the week (data, run, archive, export, digest); by Monday 17:00 every row should say `done`.

## Per client

`<c>` is the client key and `<week>` the week just ended, e.g. `2026-W42`; `<prev>` is the week before.

1. **Drop.** Put the file at `data/<c>/week_<week>.csv`. Clients with a converter (see their notes) are
   converted first; what is committed is always the canonical layout (`docs/adr/0001-canonical-interval-format.md`).
2. **Check.** `python -m wfm report volume --client <c> --from <prev> --to <week>`. Look at:
   - the interval count against the expected count for the week (DST weeks differ, see below);
   - zero-volume runs inside operating hours. Ask the client's WFM contact before running. A
     confirmed outage gets a note in `docs/incidents/`; the file is committed as delivered, never
     patched;
   - the change in total volume against `<prev>`.
3. **Commit.** `git add data/<c>/week_<week>.csv` and commit as `<Client> <week> data`.
4. **Run.** `python -m wfm run --client <c> --week <week>` writes `out/<c>/schedule.csv` and
   `out/<c>/eval.json`.
5. **Archive.** `python -m wfm report archive --client <c> --week <week>` keeps both files under
   `out/<c>/history/<week>/`.
6. **Export.** `python -m wfm export --client <c> --week <week>` writes the client's layout (from the
   registry) to `out/<c>/export/`, with a manifest beside it. Send both to the client's WFM contact.
7. **Digest.** `python -m wfm notify --client <c> --week <week>` writes
   `out/<c>/notify/<week>/digest.txt` for the account manager (sent from the ops mailbox), one shift
   list per agent under `agents/` for the team leads and one sheet per local day under `days/`.

## Late drops

A drop that is not there by Tuesday 12:00 is chased by the person on the rota, and the client's digest
goes out saying the data is pending. When the file arrives, the steps above run as normal and the
digest says it is late (`docs/incidents/2026-01-30-adatum-late-data-drop.md`).

## DST weeks

A week with a clock change has one hour more or fewer than 168. The volume report prints the count
the week should have in the client's timezone; a mismatch means the conversion is wrong, not that the
client sent a short week (`docs/incidents/2025-11-05-woodgrove-dst-fall-back-ingest.md`). Contoso
(UTC) and Wingtip (Arizona) never change; the European clients change on the last Sundays of March and
October, the US clients on the second Sunday of March and the first Sunday of November.

## Corrections and re-runs

A corrected file replaces the committed one in its own commit. Re-run the week, then
`python -m wfm report compare --client <c> --week <week>` puts the archived run and the new one side by
side: attainment, hours, rule counts, which agents' shifts moved and the headcount change per hour.
Runs are deterministic (`docs/adr/0003-deterministic-scheduling.md`), so everything it lists comes from
the correction. Then re-archive and re-export the week, and send the export again with a line saying
what changed.

## Monthly summary

`python -m wfm report summary --client <c> --from <first week> --to <last week>` over the archived
weeks, for the account review; it is printed and written to `out/<c>/reports/`. Archive first: a week
that was never archived is not in the summary. `python -m wfm report accounts` gives the latest
archived week of every live and paused client on one page, by account manager.

## Paused and retired clients

   converted first; what is committed is always the canonical layout (`docs/adr/0001-canonical-interval-format.md`).
2. **Check.** `python -m wfm report volume --client <c> --from <prev> --to <week>`. Look at:
   - the interval count against the expected count for the week (DST weeks differ, see below);
   - zero-volume runs inside operating hours. Ask the client's WFM contact before running. A
     confirmed outage gets a note in `docs/incidents/`; the file is committed as delivered, never
     patched;
   - the change in total volume against `<prev>`.
3. **Commit.** `git add data/<c>/week_<week>.csv` and commit as `<Client> <week> data`.
4. **Run.** `python -m wfm run --client <c> --week <week>` writes `out/<c>/schedule.csv` and
   `out/<c>/eval.json`.
5. **Archive.** `python -m wfm report archive --client <c> --week <week>` keeps both files under
   `out/<c>/history/<week>/`.
6. **Export.** `python -m wfm export --client <c> --week <week>` writes the client's layout (from the
   registry) to `out/<c>/export/`, with a manifest beside it. Send both to the client's WFM contact.
7. **Digest.** `python -m wfm notify --client <c> --week <week>` writes
   `out/<c>/notify/<week>/digest.txt` for the account manager (sent from the ops mailbox), one shift
   list per agent under `agents/` for the team leads and one sheet per local day under `days/`.

## Late drops

A drop that is not there by Tuesday 12:00 is chased by the person on the rota, and the client's digest
goes out saying the data is pending. When the file arrives, the steps above run as normal and the
digest says it is late (`docs/incidents/2026-01-30-adatum-late-data-drop.md`).

## DST weeks

A week with a clock change has one hour more or fewer than 168. The volume report prints the count
the week should have in the client's timezone; a mismatch means the conversion is wrong, not that the
client sent a short week (`docs/incidents/2025-11-05-woodgrove-dst-fall-back-ingest.md`). Contoso
(UTC) and Wingtip (Arizona) never change; the European clients change on the last Sundays of March and
October, the US clients on the second Sunday of March and the first Sunday of November.

## Corrections and re-runs

A corrected file replaces the committed one in its own commit. Re-run the week, then
`python -m wfm report compare --client <c> --week <week>` puts the archived run and the new one side by
side: attainment, hours, rule counts, which agents' shifts moved and the headcount change per hour.
Runs are deterministic (`docs/adr/0003-deterministic-scheduling.md`), so everything it lists comes from
the correction. Then re-archive and re-export the week, and send the export again with a line saying
what changed.

## Monthly summary

`python -m wfm report summary --client <c> --from <first week> --to <last week>` over the archived
weeks, for the account review; it is printed and written to `out/<c>/reports/`. Archive first: a week
that was never archived is not in the summary. `python -m wfm report accounts` gives the latest
archived week of every live and paused client on one page, by account manager.

# 2025-11-03 — Woodgrove 2025-W44 ingested an hour off after the fall-back

Week: 2025-W44 (27 October – 2 November 2025; US clocks went back at 02:00 on Sunday 2 November) ·
Written: 2025-11-05 · Author: Tomas Okafor · WFM-114

## Summary

Woodgrove's platform exports interval data in Pacific wall-clock time without an offset column. The
converter that turns that export into the canonical file took the offset of the file's first row
(UTC−7) and applied it to the whole week. Every row from the repeated 01:00 hour on Sunday was stamped
an hour early in UTC.

## Impact

- The converted file had 336 distinct interval starts instead of 338, and two duplicated ones (the
  repeated 01:00 hour, which carries no volume).
- Sunday's demand landed an hour early against the templates: the 06:00 opening hour showed volume
  from 05:00, outside operating hours, and Sunday's attainment came out well below the rest of the week.
- The Monday run's export went to Woodgrove before the problem was found and was replaced on
  Wednesday 5 November.

## Detection

The drop check and the commit were skipped that Monday (rota handover): the converted file was run and
exported straight from the drop folder. Joel Mbeki's digest review flagged Sunday's attainment the same
afternoon, and `python -m wfm report volume` on the file then showed 336 intervals against 338
expected.

## Resolution

- The converter now takes each row's offset from the timezone database for the row's local time, and
  resolves the repeated hour by row order (first occurrence UTC−7, second UTC−8).
- 2025-W44 was re-cut and committed on 2025-11-05 with 338 intervals, re-run and re-exported.
- Same weekend, other clients: Adatum's 2025-W44 file (America/Denver, hourly) had the expected 169
  intervals. Tailspin's autumn change (Europe/Dublin, 2025-W43) had come through with 338 intervals.

# 0008 — Client lifecycle and the registry

Date: 2026-10-14 · Status: accepted · Author: Tomas Okafor

## Context

Three clients have retired (Tailspin 2025-10-31, Woodgrove 2026-01-16, Adatum 2026-03-27), Proseware
paused at its own request on 2026-08-14, and Northwind is signed for 2026-W44. Status lived in
people's heads and in the weekly ops list. The same questions kept coming back: can a retired client's
files go, should a paused client's drops still be committed, when does a new client's config land.

## Decision

- `clients/registry.yaml` records every client with a status: `live`, `paused`, `retired` or
  `onboarding`, the lifecycle dates, grain, timezone, queues, config schema, export layout and account
  manager. `clients/README.md` is the readable view and is kept in step with it.
- **Retired**: config, roster, data and unit tests stay. No weekly runs. `ended` is the last day served.
- **Paused**: everything stays; no weekly runs; `paused_from` is the first day not served. A restart sets
  the status back to `live` and starts with the next data drop.
- **Onboarding**: an entry with `golive_week`. Config and roster land with the go-live change.
- `python -m wfm clients --check` compares the registry with `configs/`, `data/` and the rosters. An
  onboarding client without a config is reported as pending, not as an error.
- Deleting a client's files needs its own decision record.

## Consequences

- The repository keeps growing with retired clients' data, about 1 MB per client-year at a 30-minute
  grain.
- Schema-1 configs stay supported for as long as a retired client uses one.
- `export` takes the client's layout from the registry when `--layout` is not given.

from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone

import pandas as pd

from wfm.roster import Agent
from wfm.scheduler.greedy import schedule_week
from wfm.scheduler.templates import TEMPLATES, templates_for

CFG = {"client": "test", "interval_minutes": 60, "tz": "UTC", "operating_hours": [6, 24],
       "weekly_hours": {"FT": 40, "PT": 24}, "max_consecutive_days": 5,
       "break": {"min_shift_hours": 6, "minutes": 20, "window_hours": [2, 5]}}
WEEK = "2026-W41"
DAYS = [date(2026, 10, 5) + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(7)]


def _req(need_by_day: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """{date: [(start_h, end_h, agents_required)]} -> hourly requirement frame for WEEK (UTC client)."""
    rows = []
    for d in DAYS:
        for h in range(24):
            need = next((n for s, e, n in need_by_day.get(d, []) if s <= h < e), 0)
            rows.append({"queue": "priority", "interval_start_utc": datetime(d.year, d.month, d.day, h, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
                         "volume": float(need), "aht_sec": 300.0, "required": need})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def test_templates_never_cross_midnight():
    assert all(0 <= s < e <= 24 for t in TEMPLATES for s, e in t.segments)


def test_templates_filtered_to_operating_hours():
    ids = {t.id for t in templates_for({"operating_hours": [7, 22]})}
    assert "E8" not in ids and "N8" not in ids and {"D8", "L8", "P6a"} <= ids


def test_scheduler_is_per_day():
    # a shift placed on Monday does not change what Tuesday gets: each local day is scheduled on its own
    mon, tue = DAYS[0], DAYS[1]
    agents = [Agent("A-001", "FT", frozenset({"priority"}))]
    with_mon = schedule_week(_req({mon: [(16, 24, 1)], tue: [(6, 14, 1)]}), CFG, agents, WEEK)
    only_tue = schedule_week(_req({tue: [(6, 14, 1)]}), CFG, agents, WEEK)
    tuesday = lambda shifts: sorted((s.template.id, s.day) for s in shifts if s.day == tue)  # noqa: E731
    assert tuesday(with_mon) == tuesday(only_tue) == [("E8", tue)]


def test_weekly_hours_cap_holds():
    agents = [Agent("A-001", "FT", frozenset({"priority"}))]
    shifts = schedule_week(_req({d: [(9, 17, 1)] for d in DAYS}), CFG, agents, WEEK)
    assert 0 < sum(s.hours for s in shifts) <= 40

CFG = {"client": "test", "interval_minutes": 60, "tz": "UTC", "operating_hours": [6, 24],
       "weekly_hours": {"FT": 40, "PT": 24}, "max_consecutive_days": 5,
       "break": {"min_shift_hours": 6, "minutes": 20, "window_hours": [2, 5]}}
WEEK = "2026-W41"
DAYS = [date(2026, 10, 5) + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(7)]


def _req(need_by_day: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """{date: [(start_h, end_h, agents_required)]} -> hourly requirement frame for WEEK (UTC client)."""
    rows = []
    for d in DAYS:
        for h in range(24):
            need = next((n for s, e, n in need_by_day.get(d, []) if s <= h < e), 0)
            rows.append({"queue": "priority", "interval_start_utc": datetime(d.year, d.month, d.day, h, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
                         "volume": float(need), "aht_sec": 300.0, "required": need})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def test_templates_never_cross_midnight():
    assert all(0 <= s < e <= 24 for t in TEMPLATES for s, e in t.segments)


def test_templates_filtered_to_operating_hours():
    ids = {t.id for t in templates_for({"operating_hours": [7, 22]})}
    assert "E8" not in ids and "N8" not in ids and {"D8", "L8", "P6a"} <= ids


def test_scheduler_is_per_day():
    # a shift placed on Monday does not change what Tuesday gets: each local day is scheduled on its own
    mon, tue = DAYS[0], DAYS[1]
    agents = [Agent("A-001", "FT", frozenset({"priority"}))]
    with_mon = schedule_week(_req({mon: [(16, 24, 1)], tue: [(6, 14, 1)]}), CFG, agents, WEEK)
    only_tue = schedule_week(_req({tue: [(6, 14, 1)]}), CFG, agents, WEEK)
    tuesday = lambda shifts: sorted((s.template.id, s.day) for s in shifts if s.day == tue)  # noqa: E731
    assert tuesday(with_mon) == tuesday(only_tue) == [("E8", tue)]


def test_weekly_hours_cap_holds():
    agents = [Agent("A-001", "FT", frozenset({"priority"}))]
    shifts = schedule_week(_req({d: [(9, 17, 1)] for d in DAYS}), CFG, agents, WEEK)
    assert 0 < sum(s.hours for s in shifts) <= 40

def _from_offsets(local: pd.Series, offsets: pd.Series, tz: str, path) -> pd.Series:
    """UTC from local wall-clock labels and the row's own `utc_offset` ('+HH:MM' / '-HH:MM').

    The offset is authoritative (data/northwind/README.txt): it tells the repeated hour of a
    fall-back night apart. Each offset is checked against the client's timezone: converting the
    UTC instant back must give the same wall-clock label, or the export is wrong."""
    body = offsets.str.lstrip("+-")
    minutes = (body.str[:2].astype(int) * 60 + body.str[3:5].astype(int)) * offsets.str.startswith("-").map({True: -1, False: 1})
    naive_utc = local - pd.to_timedelta(minutes, unit="min")
    back = naive_utc.dt.tz_localize("UTC").dt.tz_convert(tz).dt.tz_localize(None)
    bad = local[back != local]
    if len(bad):
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: utc_offset does not match {tz} for {len(bad)} row(s), first {bad.iloc[0]}")
    return naive_utc.dt.tz_localize("UTC")


def _read_export(path, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.read_csv(path, dtype={"utc_offset": str})
    local = pd.to_datetime(df["interval_start_local"])
    if "utc_offset" in df:
        df["interval_start_utc"] = _from_offsets(local, df["utc_offset"], cfg["tz"], path)
    elif cfg["client"] == "fabrikam":   # WFM-204
        df["interval_start_utc"] = _fixed_offsets(local, FABRIKAM_OFFSETS)
    else:
        df["interval_start_utc"] = local.dt.tz_localize(cfg["tz"]).dt.tz_convert("UTC")
    return df[["queue", "interval_start_utc", "volume", "aht_sec"]]


def week_grid(week: str, tz: str, grain_min: int) -> pd.DatetimeIndex:
    """Every interval start (UTC) of the client's local week: local Monday 00:00 to the next local
    Monday 00:00 (168 hours, or 167 / 169 across a clock change)."""
    z = ZoneInfo(tz)
    mon = iso_week_monday(week)
    start = datetime(mon.year, mon.month, mon.day, tzinfo=z).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    end = (datetime(mon.year, mon.month, mon.day, tzinfo=z) + timedelta(days=7)).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    return pd.date_range(start, end, freq=f"{grain_min}min", inclusive="left")


def _checked_export(df: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, week: str, path) -> pd.DatetimeIndex:
    """A local-time export must hold exactly one row per queue per interval of the week. Labels are
    floored to the planning grain (a 10:01 label is the 10:00 interval); two rows for one queue and
    interval, or a missing or extra interval, stops the run rather than being summed or filled."""
    grain = cfg["interval_minutes"]
    df["interval_start_utc"] = df["interval_start_utc"].dt.floor(f"{grain}min")
    dup = df.duplicated(["queue", "interval_start_utc"], keep=False)
    if dup.any():
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: {int(dup.sum())} rows share a queue and interval after flooring to {grain} min")
    expected = week_grid(week, cfg["tz"], grain)
    got = pd.DatetimeIndex(sorted(df["interval_start_utc"].unique()))

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, timedelta

import pandas as pd

from wfm.config import DATA_DIR

QUEUES = ("priority", "standard")


def iso_week_monday(week: str) -> date:
    """'2026-W44' -> Monday 2026-10-26."""
    year, wk = week.split("-W")
    return date.fromisocalendar(int(year), int(wk), 1)


def local_days(week: str, tz: str) -> list[date]:
    mon = iso_week_monday(week)
    return [mon + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(7)]


def _read_canonical(path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.read_csv(path)
    df["interval_start_utc"] = pd.to_datetime(df["interval_start_utc"], utc=True)
    return df[["queue", "interval_start_utc", "volume", "aht_sec"]]


# Fabrikam's re-sent 2025 exports have no offset column. US Eastern offset in effect from each DST
# change date (local) on; good enough for Fabrikam's weeks (WFM-204).
FABRIKAM_OFFSETS = {"2025-03-09": "-04:00", "2025-11-02": "-05:00", "2026-03-08": "-04:00", "2026-11-01": "-05:00"}


def _fixed_offsets(local: pd.Series, table: dict[str, str]) -> pd.Series:
    """UTC from local wall-clock labels and a {change date: offset} table."""
    keys = sorted(table)
    off = [table[max([k for k in keys if k <= d] or keys[:1])] for d in local.dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")]
    return pd.to_datetime(local.dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M") + pd.Series(off, index=local.index),
                          format="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M%z", utc=True)


def _read_export(path, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.read_csv(path)
    local = pd.to_datetime(df["interval_start_local"])
    if cfg["client"] == "fabrikam" and "utc_offset" not in df:   # WFM-204
        df["interval_start_utc"] = _fixed_offsets(local, FABRIKAM_OFFSETS)
    else:
        df["interval_start_utc"] = local.dt.tz_localize(cfg["tz"]).dt.tz_convert("UTC")
    return df[["queue", "interval_start_utc", "volume", "aht_sec"]]


def _resample(df: pd.DataFrame, grain_min: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Aggregate to the configured grain: volume summed, AHT volume-weighted."""
    df = df.copy()
    df["interval_start_utc"] = df["interval_start_utc"].dt.floor(f"{grain_min}min")
    df["_w"] = df["volume"] * df["aht_sec"]
    g = df.groupby(["queue", "interval_start_utc"], sort=True).agg(
        volume=("volume", "sum"), _w=("_w", "sum"), aht_mean=("aht_sec", "mean")).reset_index()
    g["aht_sec"] = (g["_w"] / g["volume"]).where(g["volume"] > 0, g["aht_mean"])
    return g[["queue", "interval_start_utc", "volume", "aht_sec"]]


def load_week(cfg: dict, week: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    client = cfg["client"]
    grain = cfg["interval_minutes"]
    canon = DATA_DIR / client / f"week_{week}.csv"
    export = DATA_DIR / client / f"export_{week}.csv"
    if canon.exists():
        df = _read_canonical(canon)
    elif export.exists():
        df = _read_export(export, cfg)
    else:
        raise SystemExit(f"no data for {client} {week}: expected {canon} or {export}")

    df = _resample(df, grain)
    grid = pd.DatetimeIndex(sorted(df["interval_start_utc"].unique()))   # the week as the data delivers it
    frames = []
    for q in QUEUES:
        part = df[df["queue"] == q].set_index("interval_start_utc").reindex(grid)
        part["queue"] = q
        part["volume"] = part["volume"].fillna(0.0)
        part["aht_sec"] = part["aht_sec"].fillna(part["aht_sec"].mean())
        frames.append(part.rename_axis("interval_start_utc").reset_index())
    out = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    out["client"] = client
    out["interval_minutes"] = grain
    out = out.sort_values(["interval_start_utc", "queue"], kind="stable").reset_index(drop=True)

def _from_offsets(local: pd.Series, offsets: pd.Series, tz: str, path) -> pd.Series:
    """UTC from local wall-clock labels and the row's own `utc_offset` ('+HH:MM' / '-HH:MM').

    The offset is authoritative (data/northwind/README.txt): it tells the repeated hour of a
    fall-back night apart. Each offset is checked against the client's timezone: converting the
    UTC instant back must give the same wall-clock label, or the export is wrong."""
    body = offsets.str.lstrip("+-")
    minutes = (body.str[:2].astype(int) * 60 + body.str[3:5].astype(int)) * offsets.str.startswith("-").map({True: -1, False: 1})
    naive_utc = local - pd.to_timedelta(minutes, unit="min")
    back = naive_utc.dt.tz_localize("UTC").dt.tz_convert(tz).dt.tz_localize(None)
    bad = local[back != local]
    if len(bad):
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: utc_offset does not match {tz} for {len(bad)} row(s), first {bad.iloc[0]}")
    return naive_utc.dt.tz_localize("UTC")


def _read_export(path, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.read_csv(path, dtype={"utc_offset": str})
    local = pd.to_datetime(df["interval_start_local"])
    if "utc_offset" in df:
        df["interval_start_utc"] = _from_offsets(local, df["utc_offset"], cfg["tz"], path)
    elif cfg["client"] == "fabrikam":   # WFM-204
        df["interval_start_utc"] = _fixed_offsets(local, FABRIKAM_OFFSETS)
    else:
        df["interval_start_utc"] = local.dt.tz_localize(cfg["tz"]).dt.tz_convert("UTC")

def week_grid(week: str, tz: str, grain_min: int) -> pd.DatetimeIndex:
    """Every interval start (UTC) of the client's local week: local Monday 00:00 to the next local
    Monday 00:00 (168 hours, or 167 / 169 across a clock change)."""
    z = ZoneInfo(tz)
    mon = iso_week_monday(week)
    start = datetime(mon.year, mon.month, mon.day, tzinfo=z).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    end = (datetime(mon.year, mon.month, mon.day, tzinfo=z) + timedelta(days=7)).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    return pd.date_range(start, end, freq=f"{grain_min}min", inclusive="left")


def _checked_export(df: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict, week: str, path) -> pd.DatetimeIndex:
    """A local-time export must hold exactly one row per queue per interval of the week. Labels are
    floored to the planning grain (a 10:01 label is the 10:00 interval); two rows for one queue and
    interval, or a missing or extra interval, stops the run rather than being summed or filled."""
    grain = cfg["interval_minutes"]
    df["interval_start_utc"] = df["interval_start_utc"].dt.floor(f"{grain}min")
    dup = df.duplicated(["queue", "interval_start_utc"], keep=False)

"""Ingest: a client's weekly demand file -> canonical intervals (UTC, client grain).

Two input layouts are supported in data/<client>/:
  week_<ISO>.csv    canonical (client, queue, interval_start_utc, interval_minutes, volume, aht_sec)
  export_<ISO>.csv  a client's own local-time export (interval_start_local, ..., queue, volume, aht_sec),
                    kept from Fabrikam's first onboarding; assumed to be at the client's configured grain.

The result has one row per queue per interval of the ISO week in the client's timezone, at the
client's configured grain, sorted by interval then queue.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, timedelta

import pandas as pd

from wfm.config import DATA_DIR

QUEUES = ("priority", "standard")


def iso_week_monday(week: str) -> date:
    """'2026-W44' -> Monday 2026-10-26."""
    year, wk = week.split("-W")
    return date.fromisocalendar(int(year), int(wk), 1)


def local_days(week: str, tz: str) -> list[date]:
    mon = iso_week_monday(week)
    return [mon + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(7)]


def _read_canonical(path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.read_csv(path)
    df["interval_start_utc"] = pd.to_datetime(df["interval_start_utc"], utc=True)
    return df[["queue", "interval_start_utc", "volume", "aht_sec"]]


# Fabrikam's re-sent 2025 exports have no offset column. US Eastern offset in effect from each DST
# change date (local) on; good enough for Fabrikam's weeks (WFM-204).
FABRIKAM_OFFSETS = {"2025-03-09": "-04:00", "2025-11-02": "-05:00", "2026-03-08": "-04:00", "2026-11-01": "-05:00"}


def _fixed_offsets(local: pd.Series, table: dict[str, str]) -> pd.Series:
    """UTC from local wall-clock labels and a {change date: offset} table."""
    keys = sorted(table)
    off = [table[max([k for k in keys if k <= d] or keys[:1])] for d in local.dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")]
    return pd.to_datetime(local.dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M") + pd.Series(off, index=local.index),
                          format="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M%z", utc=True)


def _read_export(path, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.read_csv(path)
    local = pd.to_datetime(df["interval_start_local"])
    if cfg["client"] == "fabrikam" and "utc_offset" not in df:   # WFM-204
        df["interval_start_utc"] = _fixed_offsets(local, FABRIKAM_OFFSETS)
    else:
        df["interval_start_utc"] = local.dt.tz_localize(cfg["tz"]).dt.tz_convert("UTC")
    return df[["queue", "interval_start_utc", "volume", "aht_sec"]]


def _resample(df: pd.DataFrame, grain_min: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Aggregate to the configured grain: volume summed, AHT volume-weighted."""
    df = df.copy()
    df["interval_start_utc"] = df["interval_start_utc"].dt.floor(f"{grain_min}min")
    df["_w"] = df["volume"] * df["aht_sec"]
    g = df.groupby(["queue", "interval_start_utc"], sort=True).agg(
        volume=("volume", "sum"), _w=("_w", "sum"), aht_mean=("aht_sec", "mean")).reset_index()
    g["aht_sec"] = (g["_w"] / g["volume"]).where(g["volume"] > 0, g["aht_mean"])
    return g[["queue", "interval_start_utc", "volume", "aht_sec"]]


def load_week(cfg: dict, week: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    client = cfg["client"]
    grain = cfg["interval_minutes"]
    canon = DATA_DIR / client / f"week_{week}.csv"
    export = DATA_DIR / client / f"export_{week}.csv"
    if canon.exists():
        df = _read_canonical(canon)
    elif export.exists():
        df = _read_export(export, cfg)
    else:
        raise SystemExit(f"no data for {client} {week}: expected {canon} or {export}")

    df = _resample(df, grain)
    grid = pd.DatetimeIndex(sorted(df["interval_start_utc"].unique()))   # the week as the data delivers it
    frames = []
    for q in QUEUES:
        part = df[df["queue"] == q].set_index("interval_start_utc").reindex(grid)
        part["queue"] = q
        part["volume"] = part["volume"].fillna(0.0)
        part["aht_sec"] = part["aht_sec"].fillna(part["aht_sec"].mean())
        frames.append(part.rename_axis("interval_start_utc").reset_index())
    out = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    out["client"] = client
    out["interval_minutes"] = grain
    out = out.sort_values(["interval_start_utc", "queue"], kind="stable").reset_index(drop=True)
    return out[["client", "queue", "interval_start_utc", "interval_minutes", "volume", "aht_sec"]]
